claims.text: A machine-learning pipeline integrating compositional and microstructural descriptors can predict low lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional simplified models.
The proposed pipeline is trained using DFT-calculated anharmonic phonon properties and targeted experimental thermal-conductivity measurements.
The pipeline can reliably identify HEAs with lattice thermal conductivity below approximately 1 W/mK.
Some high-entropy alloys exhibit lattice thermal conductivity below 1 W/mK at room temperature.
The DFT outputs used by the pipeline capture full anharmonic phonon scattering.
Anharmonic phonon scattering is significant in HEAs over 300–700 K.
Lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys reduces phonon velocity and enhances phonon scattering.
Point defects enhance phonon scattering in HEAs.
Compositional fluctuations enhance phonon scattering in HEAs.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by HEA lattice distortion lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Increasing temperature within 300–700 K increases phonon scattering and decreases lattice thermal conductivity.
DFT-computed anharmonic descriptors capture the relevant electronic and phononic interactions.
Combining DFT descriptors with experimental microstructural descriptors enables the model to identify subtle trends associated with enhanced phonon scattering.
The integrated approach will reduce prediction error by approximately 20% relative to traditional models.
Combining machine learning with complementary modeling approaches can successfully predict some HEA properties.
The proposed approach is primarily applicable to HEAs at or above room temperature where anharmonic scattering is important.
The approach may not generalize to simpler alloys or low-temperature regimes.
The available experimental dataset is currently too limited to establish a 20% improvement or generalization across all HEA compositions.
Experimental lattice thermal conductivity over 300–700 K, sound velocity, and microstructure can be measured to benchmark the predictions.
Failure to obtain lattice thermal conductivity below 1 W/mK consistently, or failure to improve prediction error by roughly 20% over traditional models, would falsify the hypothesis.
